newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican bombers target ministry's holiday camp.
newsitem.headline: Corsican bombers target ministry's holiday camp.

text.p: Two bombs shook a holiday village reserved for employees of the French Justice Ministry on Corsica early on Thursday, badly damaging a communal kitchen and a bar but causing no injuries, police said.
Numerous ministry employees were at the holiday camp at the time the blasts went off at about 5 a.m. (0300 GMT), but their villas were far enough away to be out of range, the police said.
No one immediately claimed responsibility for the bombings, but police said they appeared to be part of a fresh wave of separatist violence on the French Mediterranean island since mid-August.
Bombs have exploded on the holiday island every night since the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) Historic Wing called off a shaky truce three weeks ago.
The new blasts marked the second attack against the ministry's holiday village in six years. The FLNC claimed responsibility for the first bombing, which took place in 1990.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe has ordered a crackdown on separatist guerrillas operating on the island, resulting in a flurry of recent arrests.
French police detained three people on the island on Wednesday in connection with a car bomb that killed a nationalist leader last July.
